statement: Before acting on a named project, resolve its repositories, roles, inherited instructions, and configured paths via sgt-context rather than inferring ownership from the current working directory.
trigger: any task naming or implying a project
outcome: repository ownership and instructions are established before mutation
notes: Old mechanism is the sgt-context script; the durable rule is resolve-before-act, not the script itself.
rationale: Broad, stage-independent rule that applies before any procedure begins; matches the proposal's 6.1 examples (search catalog before inventing procedure).
alternatives_considered: shared-context (since sgt-context's resolution order is itself captured as shared-context elsewhere)

statement: The primary session coordinates multi-repository work by default; it may implement directly only when the user explicitly asks to work in-session or not to dispatch, and one repository owns the complete outcome.
trigger: any task requiring an execution mode decision
outcome: coordinator vs direct-executor role is established
rationale: Applies independent of any single procedure's stage; it is the standing default that governs which workflow (dispatch-mode or direct-mode) is even eligible.
alternatives_considered: workflow trigger for a 'select-execution-mode' workflow

statement: Use dispatch mode when work spans repositories, contains two or more independent repository-owned tasks, needs an isolated independent review worker, or the user asks for workers.
trigger: one of the four listed conditions holds
outcome: dispatch mode is selected as the executing procedure
notes: Overlaps with P5's skills/dispatch/SKILL.md and skills/cross-repo-work/SKILL.md, which own the procedure this triggers.
rationale: Recognizable trigger with a bounded, invokable outcome (dispatch a fleet) — meets the 6.2 test for a reusable procedural outcome.
alternatives_considered: agents-invariant (mode-selection policy)
stage-context of a higher select-execution-mode workflow

statement: In dispatch mode, load context, plan, and decompose the requested outcome by repository before dispatching.
trigger: dispatch mode selected
outcome: work is decomposed per repository prior to dispatch
notes: Overlaps with cross-repo-work skill (P5).
rationale: A durable checkpoint operators would care whether it completed before any worker exists.
alternatives_considered: helper step inside dispatch-mode

statement: In dispatch mode, dispatch one worker per owning repository using sgt-dispatch.
trigger: decomposition complete
outcome: one isolated worker exists per owning repository
rationale: Meaningful checkpoint: fleet existence is exactly what later monitoring/reconciliation stages depend on.
alternatives_considered: helper (sgt-dispatch is a P6 mechanism)

statement: In dispatch mode, monitor progress and reconcile merge order, PRs, and cross-repository implications.
trigger: workers dispatched
outcome: cross-repository delivery is reconciled
rationale: Distinct durable checkpoint (delivery reconciliation) separate from dispatch itself.

statement: Use direct mode only when the user explicitly requests it and the work has one clear owning repository.
trigger: explicit user request plus single-repository ownership
outcome: direct mode is selected as the executing procedure
rationale: Recognizable trigger and bounded outcome (an implemented, delivered change in one repository) — a reusable procedural outcome.
alternatives_considered: agents-invariant

statement: In direct mode, run sgt-context for the project and td context for the owning task before making any edit.
trigger: direct mode selected
outcome: task and repository context are loaded before mutation

statement: In direct mode, reconcile existing workers and preserved worktrees before editing; never duplicate or race work already in progress.
trigger: task context loaded
outcome: no duplicate or racing work is created

statement: In direct mode, claim or create the owning td task, then implement test-driven-first in the requested checkout or an isolated worktree.
trigger: no conflicting work found
outcome: implementation proceeds under an owned, tracked task

statement: In direct mode, never edit a default branch; create or reuse the owning feature branch before the first implementation change.
trigger: implementation about to begin
outcome: all direct-mode changes land on a feature branch, never on default
rationale: A specific, checkable prohibition scoped to the implement checkpoint of direct mode rather than a standalone procedure.
alternatives_considered: agents-invariant given its severity as a safety rule

statement: In direct mode, run repository-native validation, independent reviews, and the final shipping gate exactly as a dispatched worker would.
trigger: implementation complete
outcome: direct-mode changes pass the same gates a dispatched worker's changes would
notes: Establishes parity between direct and dispatch mode outcomes; do not treat direct mode as a lighter-weight path.

statement: In direct mode, open a PR for every implementation and satisfy required CI, review threads, and merge authorization before calling delivery complete.
trigger: validation passed
outcome: delivery is not declared complete until PR/CI/review/merge conditions are met

statement: In direct mode, record handoff, PR, merge, deployment, and cleanup outcomes.
trigger: delivery complete
outcome: delivery outcomes are durably recorded

statement: Never use the coordinator role as a reason to stop at a plan, status report, or dispatch suggestion when the user asked for an implemented outcome.
trigger: user requested an implemented outcome
outcome: the coordinator does not substitute a plan for delivery
rationale: Broad prohibition independent of which mode or stage is active; matches the 6.1 style directly.

statement: Never use direct mode to edit several repositories in one checkout, or to bypass repository instructions, task ownership, review independence, or shipping gates.
trigger: direct mode selected
outcome: direct mode cannot be used to circumvent multi-repo or gate discipline
rationale: A prohibition specific to direct mode's boundaries, not a universal invariant independent of mode.
alternatives_considered: agents-invariant

statement: Every directive in an agent-instruction file must specify at least one observable element: a trigger/condition, a required/prohibited action, or evidence/a stop condition proving compliance.
trigger: authoring or reviewing an instruction file
outcome: every directive is checkable
notes: This is a meta-rule about how the corpus itself (including this very partition's source files) must be written.
rationale: Broad, stage-independent editorial invariant governing all instruction surfaces.

statement: Do not add directives such as "be thorough," "write clean code," or "use best practices"; replace them with named commands, failure behavior, acceptance criteria, ownership, or review evidence, and remove any sentence that cannot change a decision or be checked afterward.
trigger: authoring or reviewing an instruction file
outcome: vague, unenforceable directives are removed or replaced
rationale: Same class as the preceding unit; kept separate because it names a distinct, independently checkable rule (banning vague phrasing) rather than the positive requirement.

statement: If a toolbelt command covers an operation, use it instead of reproducing the operation with ad hoc shell commands.
trigger: an operation is about to be performed
outcome: the canonical script, not an improvised command sequence, performs the operation
notes: The specific toolbelt commands themselves are P6 (bin/ machinery); this unit is the precedence rule.
rationale: Broad rule independent of which stage or workflow is executing.

statement: Fall back to manual operations only when no toolbelt command covers the operation or the command returns an explicit unsupported-case error; report that fallback and preserve the original error evidence.
trigger: no covering command exists, or it fails with an explicit unsupported error
outcome: any manual fallback is reported with preserved evidence, never silent
rationale: Broad rule independent of stage; a direct extension of the preceding precedence rule.

statement: Load procedures (skills) only when their trigger applies.
trigger: a task is presented
outcome: irrelevant skills are never loaded speculatively
notes: Echoed verbatim in docs/skills.md L3-4 (same partition, separate file) — likely the same source concept restated; keep both citations for provenance.
rationale: Matches the 6.1 'search the workflow catalog before inventing a procedure' example almost exactly.

statement: Sergeant-owned procedural skills live at skills/<name>/SKILL.md and Sergeant-authored worker skills live at .agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md; for every listed trigger, read that repository-local file directly — it is canonical and takes precedence over any same-named registry skill.
trigger: a listed trigger applies
outcome: the repository-local file, not a registry copy, governs behavior
rationale: Broad authority rule independent of which specific skill or stage is in play.

statement: A harness registry may assist loading a skill, but its omission does not make the skill unavailable; do not ask the owner or stop solely because the registry omits the skill.
trigger: a registry does not list an expected skill
outcome: loading proceeds from the repository-local file regardless of registry state
rationale: Fail-forward rule independent of stage.

statement: Only stop and report the exact repository-local path when that file is absent or unreadable; do not reconstruct a partial protocol from memory.
trigger: the repository-local skill file cannot be found or read
outcome: the actor stops and reports the exact missing path rather than improvising from memory
rationale: Fail-closed rule independent of stage; mirrors the runtime's own 'ambiguity fails closed' invariant (CLAUDE.md).

statement: Any task the user brings triggers a nine-step standard workflow: load context, check the task queue, choose an execution mode, reconcile existing state, confirm only unresolved decisions, execute, monitor real progress, handle decision gates, and reconcile and deliver.

source.locator: AGENTS.md L132-146, Standard workflow heading and steps

trigger: the user brings any task
outcome: the task proceeds through context, mode selection, execution, and reconciled delivery
notes: This is the top-level orchestration procedure the rest of AGENTS.md's mode-specific rules plug into.
rationale: Recognizable trigger (any task), an ordered bounded sequence, and an explicit completion condition (reconciled delivery) — squarely a reusable procedural outcome per 6.2.
alternatives_considered: agents-invariant (too broad; misses the ordered-checkpoint structure)

statement: Load context: run sgt-context and identify the owning repository or repositories, inherited instructions, configured paths, and cross-repository dependencies before selecting an execution mode.
trigger: a task has been brought
outcome: project/repository context is established before mode selection

statement: Check the queue: run sgt-td-list and reuse a matching task in direct or dispatch mode; create a task only when no canonical task exists.
trigger: context loaded
outcome: duplicate task creation is avoided

statement: Choose execution mode: direct for explicit single-repository work in this session; dispatch for cross-repository, parallel, or explicitly delegated work.
trigger: queue checked
outcome: an execution mode is selected before further action

statement: Reconcile existing state: run sgt-watch --sync-all, then inspect active workers, branches, worktrees, retained gates, and handoffs before starting; resume or take over preserved work rather than creating duplicates.
trigger: an execution mode is chosen
outcome: no preserved work is duplicated or abandoned

statement: Confirm only unresolved decisions that change scope or risk: ask only when repository ownership, user-visible behavior, security/privacy policy, data retention, destructive action, or an irreversible tradeoff is unknown; do not ask the user to reconfirm an execution mode, plan, or tradeoff already recorded in the conversation or td.
trigger: state reconciled
outcome: the user is asked only for genuinely missing, risk-changing decisions
rationale: This is a judgment checkpoint (what counts as 'unresolved' and 'risk-changing') requiring an actor's evaluation, not a deterministic helper.
alternatives_considered: stage (bare durable checkpoint)

statement: Execute: in direct mode, start the td task and implement through tests, review, and delivery; in dispatch mode, run sgt-dispatch with a repository list or a td id.
trigger: decisions confirmed
outcome: the chosen mode's procedure begins

statement: Monitor real progress: require recent meaningful events or an active child operation plus exact pane/process identity — parent-process liveness alone is insufficient; in OpenCode use a managed background watch and verify it started, falling back to bounded one-shot status checks rather than a blocking watch call when unavailable.
trigger: execution has begun
outcome: progress claims are backed by verified, recent, identity-bound evidence
rationale: Carries a durable evidentiary standard ('recent meaningful events' plus exact identity) that any reimplementation must still satisfy for the checkpoint to mean anything.

statement: Handle decisions: for needs_input, blocked, or ask-user gates, read the exact finding, obtain only genuinely missing user decisions, record them in td, and continue approved remediation without asking again merely to dispatch.
trigger: a decision gate is hit
outcome: the gate is resolved with a recorded decision, not re-asked repeatedly
notes: Directly relevant to the proposal's needs_input semantics (U3).
rationale: Requires judgment to distinguish a genuinely missing decision from an already-recorded one.

statement: Reconcile and deliver: surface PRs and merge order, complete approved merges/deployments, and run cleanup only after terminal state and preserved evidence are verified.
trigger: execution and decisions are resolved
outcome: delivery is reconciled and cleanup is safe

statement: Workers use in_progress, needs_input, blocked, and waiting as nonterminal states.
trigger: a worker exists
outcome: state is described with a closed, known vocabulary of nonterminal states
rationale: A vocabulary reused by monitoring, decision-handling, and recovery procedures alike; not itself a checkpoint.

statement: A waiting worker may remain alive or may exit after a durable handoff; deferred waits should publish .sergeant-wake-condition and resume through sgt-wake, while human decisions still resume through sgt-respond.
trigger: a worker enters the waiting state
outcome: resumption uses the correct one of two distinct durable paths depending on whether the wait is a deferred condition or a human decision
rationale: Precursor evidence for proposal's needs_input/waiting semantics (§15.4); reused across dispatch, direct, and recovery contexts.

statement: Do not infer progress from liveness, do not rewrite an expected blocked exit as orphaned, and do not clean a waiting worktree.
trigger: a worker is blocked or waiting
outcome: blocked/waiting workers are neither treated as active nor prematurely reclaimed
rationale: Three independent, broadly-applicable prohibitions about worker-state interpretation.

statement: Use sgt-respond, sgt-wake, or supported recovery only after reconciling status, response generation, pane identity, and handoff evidence.
trigger: a resume action is about to be taken
outcome: resumption never proceeds on stale or unverified evidence
rationale: A precondition gating the same handle-decisions/reconcile checkpoints described elsewhere in the standard workflow.

statement: Every dispatched implementation, independent review, PR description, successor, recovery, and final shipping gate must use the same canonical intent revision from .sergeant-intent.md.
trigger: any of the listed actions occurs for a piece of work
outcome: all actions on a piece of work trace to one canonical, content-addressed intent revision
rationale: A single artifact (.sergeant-intent.md, content-hash revisioned per bin/_sgt-intent.sh, P6) referenced by name across many otherwise-independent procedures — the textbook shared-context case.
alternatives_considered: shared-helper

statement: Workers and remediation loops never run no-mistakes.
trigger: a worker or remediation loop is active
outcome: no-mistakes is invoked only by the coordinator, never by a worker
rationale: A strict ownership boundary independent of which specific workflow is running; also echoed in README's no-mistakes section and repo-scoped-skills.md.

statement: After readiness, the coordinator uses sgt-validate to launch the single validation-only boundary in a split pane of the worker's tmux window.
trigger: a worker reaches readiness
outcome: exactly one coordinator-owned validation boundary is launched per readiness
notes: The durable rule is 'exactly one coordinator-owned validation boundary'; 'split pane of the worker's tmux window' is old Sergeant's mechanism and belongs in obsolete-mechanisms.md, not the durable procedure.
rationale: The single-validation-boundary policy is reused by both dispatch-mode and direct-mode delivery.
alternatives_considered: obsolete-mechanism for the pane-splitting half; split into two units rather than one to keep the durable half faithfully separated per the source-inventory's guidance

statement: sgt-validate's default medium profile skips the redundant no-mistakes review and document stages.
trigger: a validation boundary is launched with the default profile
outcome: review/document stages are not duplicated when the coordinator already covered them
rationale: A configuration detail of one profile rather than an independent checkpoint or reusable procedure.

statement: Remediation that changes HEAD still requires independent rereview before updating the readiness marker, but must not trigger repeated no-mistakes review cycles.
trigger: remediation changes HEAD after an initial validation pass
outcome: rereview happens exactly once per remediation without re-running the whole gate
rationale: A durable checkpoint rule (rereview required) paired with an efficiency constraint (no repeated cycles) scoped to this workflow.

statement: A plan, task, finding, or worker launch is not the requested outcome unless the user asked only for planning or dispatch.
trigger: work concludes
outcome: delivery is judged against what the user actually asked for, not against process artifacts
rationale: Broad, stage-independent completion-criteria rule.

statement: Do not repeatedly report a known blocker after its decision and remediation path are approved; execute the next safe step.
trigger: a blocker has already been decided and its remediation approved
outcome: execution proceeds instead of re-reporting the same blocker

statement: Do not create duplicate tasks, findings, PRs, workers, or review passes when a canonical preserved owner exists.
trigger: a canonical owner already exists for a task/finding/PR/worker/review
outcome: no duplicate artifact is created

statement: Do not call a worker active solely because its process or pane exists; require recent meaningful progress evidence.
trigger: worker liveness is being assessed
outcome: activity claims require evidence beyond bare process existence
notes: Same evidentiary standard as the standard-workflow monitor step (L144) and the canonical Worker definition in docs/what-is-sergeant.md.

statement: Do not leave a completed, merged, blocked, or abandoned task recorded as in_progress; reconcile td and fleet state truthfully.
trigger: a task's real state diverges from its recorded state
outcome: recorded state is corrected to match reality

statement: Tool absence should produce an actionable fallback or explicit blocker, not a silent skip, false success, or indefinite wait.
trigger: a required tool is unavailable
outcome: the absence is surfaced explicitly rather than hidden
rationale: Fail-closed/fail-loud rule consistent with the runtime's own ambiguity-fails-closed invariant.

statement: Standing authorization may remove repetitive dispatch confirmation, but never authorizes risk acceptance, gate skipping, force operations, secret exposure, or destruction of preserved state.
trigger: standing authorization has been granted
outcome: certain risk classes remain non-delegable regardless of standing authorization
rationale: A safety ceiling that cannot be lifted even by broad prior authorization; high-severity, stage-independent.

statement: dev_root is set in ~/.config/sergeant/config.yaml; repository paths in project YAMLs are relative to it.
trigger: resolving a repository path from a project YAML
outcome: the same relative-path convention applies to every project
rationale: A single resolution rule referenced wherever any repository path is resolved, across load-project, dispatch, and sync alike.

statement: A project's name is its YAML filename without extension (smith.yaml → project smith).
trigger: identifying a project by name
outcome: project identity is derived deterministically from the registry filename

statement: sgt-context resolves instructions in order: defaults.agent_instructions, then group instructions, then repository instructions; later layers override earlier ones for the same repository.
trigger: instructions for a repository are being assembled
outcome: a single deterministic override order governs every repository's effective instructions
rationale: Textbook shared-context: one resolution algorithm consumed by every workflow that needs a repository's effective instructions.

statement: Never modify repositories under ~/.config/sergeant/ — that is configuration, not code.
trigger: any file operation touches ~/.config/sergeant/
outcome: the registry itself is never treated as an editable code repository

statement: Never commit secrets; project YAMLs may contain paths but should not contain credentials.
trigger: authoring or editing a project YAML or any commit
outcome: credentials never enter version control via Sergeant's own configuration

statement: Use a bare sgt-* command when it resolves on PATH; otherwise run the matching script from this repository's bin/ directory.
trigger: invoking any sgt-* operation
outcome: the same operation resolves consistently whether or not the toolbelt is installed on PATH
notes: A PATH-resolution detail distinct from, but closely related to, the general toolbelt-precedence rule (L60-61).
alternatives_considered: helper

statement: SERGEANT_AGENT or sgt-dispatch --agent may select opencode, oc, goose, claude, or an equivalent path whose basename is one of those names; dispatch uses only persistent interactive sessions and rejects every other agent and all non-interactive launch modes before creating worker state.
trigger: a dispatch is requested
outcome: only a known interactive harness can ever get as far as creating worker state
notes: A validate-before-any-side-effect pattern; directly relevant to the proposal's harness registry/capability gate (§17).
rationale: A judgment/validation checkpoint gating the dispatch-mode workflow's entry, not a standalone reusable outcome by itself.

statement: sgt-dispatch --model or SERGEANT_MODEL pins the harness model as provider/model[:variant]; --agent/SERGEANT_AGENT select the executable and are orthogonal to it; precedence is --model > SERGEANT_MODEL > the harness's ambient default, and an unpinned dispatch is recorded as unpinned rather than left blank.
trigger: a dispatch is being launched
outcome: the resolved model tuple and its provenance (or explicit absence) are always recorded
rationale: Durable launch-evidence requirement; direct precedent for the proposal's executor-aware ExecutionRecord (§13.4).

statement: Transports are per-harness and measured, not inferred: a harness that is not installed is recorded as unmeasured rather than unsupported.
trigger: resolving how a harness accepts a model/variant pin
outcome: capability claims are backed by measurement, never assumed from documentation
notes: Directly echoes this repository's own L1 lesson (measure the CLI, never assume).
rationale: A measurement doctrine independent of any one stage — applies to every harness capability claim anywhere in the system.

statement: A model/variant tuple the selected harness cannot honor fails before any intent file, td task, worktree, or fleet state is created, and a worker handed one fails terminally instead of inheriting the ambient default.
trigger: a pinned tuple cannot be honored by the selected harness
outcome: no partial or silently-degraded worker state is ever created
rationale: Fail-closed checkpoint gating dispatch-mode's entry, consistent with the runtime's own ambiguity-fails-closed invariant.

statement: sgt-dispatch --managed-coordinator-pane or --coordinator-pane <pane-id> let a coordinator not inside tmux bind a coordinator pane; the two cannot be combined, the managed path never starts a tmux server, and every path verifies the pane against the live server before use.
trigger: a coordinator outside tmux needs to bind a pane before dispatching
outcome: an absent, stale, or forged pane identity is refused rather than adopted
notes: The durable intent — never trust an unverified execution-context identity — is what must survive; tmux pane binding itself is the mechanism D2 already rules the sergeant-rs daemon replaces structurally (no TTY/pane at all). Kept in decompose per the source-inventory's rule for dense tmux content.
rationale: D2 (GAUNTLET.md deviation register) already establishes the daemon has no TTY/pane; the entire pane-binding channel this rule protects does not exist in sergeant-rs, so the mechanism is superseded even though the underlying 'verify identity before trust' intent is durable and should reappear wherever the daemon establishes an execution context's identity.
alternatives_considered: stage-context of dispatch-mode (kept as durable procedure)
engine-gap (rejected: the identity-verification intent is already satisfied structurally by the daemon's exclusive process-handle ownership, not missing)

statement: The right unit of distribution for turning a general-purpose agent into a specialist is not a CLI tool or an MCP server, but a cloned directory of instructions, skills, and conventions.
trigger: designing how Sergeant is distributed and adopted
outcome: Sergeant ships as a cloned instruction/skills directory, not a packaged tool or server
notes: Attributed to firstmate's precedent; the actual claim is a distribution-model invariant Sergeant itself follows.
rationale: A standing architectural commitment independent of any procedure or stage.

statement: Sergeant narrows firstmate's crew-orchestration idea to start from project topology: a project is a named collection of repositories, and everything (context, instructions, dispatch, graphify output) flows from that definition.
trigger: scoping what Sergeant is for
outcome: Sergeant's entire behavior is organized around the project-of-repositories concept

statement: Sergeant is an agent distro — a cloned directory with an AGENTS.md, shell toolbelt, and skills — that turns a general-purpose agent into a project-aware first mate once launched inside it.
trigger: an agent harness is launched inside the Sergeant directory
outcome: the harness gains project awareness (repos, grouping, applicable instructions) without further install

statement: No install step is required — the cloned repository is the distro — and Sergeant supports Bash 3.2 and newer, including the system Bash shipped with macOS.
trigger: running any Sergeant script
outcome: scripts remain correct on the oldest supported Bash without requiring installation
notes: Strong portable evidence for the proposal's §18 cross-platform contract; also explains why P7 has a dedicated Bash-3.2 regression test.

statement: The project registry (~/.config/sergeant/, one YAML per project plus global config), the developer's own repositories, and the Sergeant distro itself (AGENTS.md, bin/, skills/) are three distinct, separately-located directory trees that together define a project's context.
trigger: establishing what a 'project' is made of
outcome: context resolution always draws from exactly these three trees
rationale: The structural shape every context-resolution procedure (sgt-context, load-project) depends on.

statement: Each project is one YAML file defining which repositories belong to it, how they group, where Sergeant publishes merged graphify output, and what agent instructions apply per group and per repository.
trigger: defining or reading a project
outcome: a project's full definition is contained in one file
notes: Overlaps with docs/schema.md (P8), which owns the full schema; this is the top-level shape only.

statement: Use no-mistakes as a final shipping gate, not an implementation loop; implementation, focused repository-native tests, lint, and independent review must be complete before starting it.
trigger: a change is ready to ship
outcome: no-mistakes only ever runs after all other validation is already complete
rationale: The defining ownership boundary for the whole no-mistakes-shipping-gate workflow; echoed in P2's no-mistakes skill and AGENTS.md L152.

statement: A clean no-mistakes run takes several minutes; invoking it during development or repeatedly restarting it multiplies that cost.
trigger: considering whether to (re)start a no-mistakes run
outcome: runs are started deliberately, not repeatedly, to avoid multiplying cost

statement: Before starting a run: finish and commit on a feature branch, ensure no-mistakes doctor is healthy, and check no-mistakes axi for an already-active matching run — reattach rather than create a duplicate.
trigger: about to start a no-mistakes run
outcome: no duplicate concurrent run is created and preconditions are verified

statement: A run may be started from an intent file (--intent-file) or an inline intent string (--intent).
trigger: starting a no-mistakes run
outcome: either invocation form produces an equivalent run against the same intent
rationale: A deterministic invocation detail subordinate to the start-run checkpoint, not itself a checkpoint.

statement: Do not use --yes; use --skip=<steps> only for stages already proven irrelevant — skipping is not a substitute for checks that have not been performed.
trigger: starting or configuring a no-mistakes run
outcome: gate steps are never bulk-approved or skipped without proven irrelevance

statement: Routine dispatched workers do not invoke no-mistakes for ordinary completion, prototypes, investigations, documentation drafts, intermediate commits, or remediation loops; the coordinator starts a single run only after the implementation branch is committed and native validation is complete.
trigger: any worker completes any of the listed non-final activities
outcome: no-mistakes is never invoked except by the coordinator for a single final run
rationale: Restates and sharpens AGENTS.md L152's ownership boundary with an explicit enumerated exclusion list.

statement: axi run and axi respond block while work is active — a quiet step is not a stall; check progress with axi status without issuing duplicate run commands.
trigger: a run appears quiet
outcome: progress is checked without ever issuing a second, duplicate run command

statement: At each gate, inspect every finding: auto-fix findings are authorized selectively after review; ask-user findings are relayed to the user and never approved, fixed, or skipped autonomously; no-op findings are informational and the gate is simply approved.
trigger: a gate presents findings
outcome: each finding is handled according to its category, with human authority preserved for ask-user findings
rationale: A judgment checkpoint (classify and act per finding) — an actor stage requiring inspection, not deterministic machinery.

statement: While a run is active: do not edit the pipeline-owned worktree, do not abort or rerun to escape a gate, and preserve all pipeline-created commits; abort only when intentionally discarding the entire run.
trigger: a run is active
outcome: the pipeline-owned worktree and commit history stay intact for the run's duration

statement: Stop driving at checks-passed: the PR is ready and no-mistakes monitors it in the background, so do not poll or wait for merge.
trigger: a run reaches checks-passed
outcome: coordinator involvement ends at checks-passed rather than continuing through merge

statement: If the outcome is failed or cancelled, inspect branch_sync state first: sync means run axi sync, continue_active_run means keep driving the reported run, and recover_custody means run axi sync --recover.
trigger: a run ends failed or cancelled
outcome: the correct one of three remediation paths is chosen deterministically from branch_sync state
rationale: A deterministic state-to-action lookup used within the finish/remediation checkpoint, not itself a checkpoint.

statement: Never improvise a reset, stash, force-push, or branch replacement around a blocked sync state.
trigger: branch_sync is blocked
outcome: recovery only ever uses the three named remediation paths, never an improvised git operation

statement: The no-mistakes run is validation-only and must not fix findings; actionable findings are routed into separate, deduplicated owning-repository td tasks with sgt-no-mistakes-finding.
trigger: a no-mistakes run produces findings
outcome: findings become tracked, deduplicated repository work rather than being fixed in-run

statement: Each finding requires an explicit --disposition: gate creates/updates P1 work and retains the gate, ask-user creates/updates P1 work and preserves human escalation, td creates/updates nonblocking actionable debt, and ignore records that no card is needed; warning debt becomes P2 and informational debt becomes P3.
trigger: routing one no-mistakes finding
outcome: every finding maps deterministically to exactly one disposition and priority
rationale: A deterministic classification table shared with P6's sgt-no-mistakes-finding, which is the mechanism that enforces it.

statement: Repeated finding IDs update the same card while retaining the latest run ID, head SHA, location, description, and originating intent; reruns also preserve any existing repo-specific or manually added td labels while ensuring the required no-mistakes and finding labels remain present without duplication.
trigger: a finding recurs across reruns
outcome: the same durable card is updated in place with fresh evidence, never duplicated, and labels are neither lost nor duplicated

statement: On rerun, visible active cards stay in their current state, while explicitly hidden states are resurfaced: closed cards are reopened and deferred cards are undeferred before the finding body is refreshed.
trigger: a finding is rerouted on rerun
outcome: a closed or deferred card is never silently left stale — it is resurfaced before the body updates
notes: This idempotent upsert-with-resurface semantics resembles the kind of durable-fact ownership the journal already provides natively; still representable via the existing td-plus-digest mechanism, so not treated as an engine-gap here.

statement: Correctness, security, data-integrity, and test findings cannot be deferred or ignored; cosmetic and evidence-only findings never create cards.
trigger: classifying a finding's category
outcome: certain finding categories are never allowed to be silently deferred, ignored, or over-tracked

statement: Generated worker briefs require one independent review per axis named in SGT_REVIEW_AXES_REQUIRED — Standards, Spec, and Readiness always, plus a conditional Accessibility axis whenever frontend/UI/visual/interaction/accessibility/user-facing language appears in the mission, repo role, or repo group — and that one definition drives both the brief's requirement and sgt-review-findings' accepted axes so the two cannot drift.

source.locator: README.md L314, review axes single source

trigger: generating a worker brief or routing a review finding
outcome: the same single vocabulary of required axes governs both what is demanded and what is accepted
rationale: A single named definition explicitly reused by two otherwise-independent procedures — the canonical shared-context case.

statement: Dispatched workers pass each axis's strict JSON finding artifact to sgt-review-findings, which creates or updates one owning-repository td task per actionable finding, preserves active task state on reruns, and publishes blocking task IDs and remediation guidance through .sergeant-message, .sergeant-status, and sgt-notify; cosmetic and false-positive dispositions create no cards.
trigger: a worker's independent review completes
outcome: actionable review findings become tracked work with published remediation guidance, without duplicating cards

statement: Findings set a canonical severity of error, warning, or info; the router also normalizes the spellings reviewers actually emit (blocker/critical/high → error/P1, major/medium → warning/P2, minor/low/informational → info/P3), and only the error family publishes a blocking gate.
trigger: routing a review finding
outcome: any spelling of severity a reviewer emits normalizes to exactly one of three canonical severities with one matching priority
notes: Matches source-inventory's bin/_sgt-review-axes.sh helper-evidence entry, which is the canonical vocabulary source.

statement: Deduplication of review findings is scoped to the owning repository, axis, source, finding id, parent mission, and branch, so two sessions cannot collide on a generic finding id.
trigger: routing a review finding
outcome: findings from different sessions never collide merely by sharing a finding id

statement: Each routed revision ends with a Revision block digest over its own bytes so a later route can tell whether the stored revision is still exactly what the router wrote; if anything changed it, the whole stored revision is preserved below a Superseded revision separator and the card is labelled needs-reconciliation, a label only a human clears once the two accounts are merged, and a closed card matching a finding is always reopened rather than abandoned, with the reopen always reported.
trigger: a routed finding's card may have been hand-edited since last write
outcome: no external edit to a finding card is ever silently overwritten; conflicting accounts are preserved and flagged for human reconciliation
notes: A durable versioning/conflict-preservation pattern with strong resemblance to journal-native event sourcing, but achieved here via an external tracker plus a content digest — representable at the helper rung, so not claimed as an engine gap.

statement: When a route fails after parsing, sanitized findings are retained under <worktree>/.sergeant-review-artifacts/<axis>-<source>/ holding only post-redaction fields, the blocked message names the exact retry command, a retry re-validates every field and recomputes each content digest, and a route refuses to overwrite an artifact nobody has retried yet.
trigger: a review route fails after parsing
outcome: a failed route always leaves a named, safely-retryable artifact rather than losing or silently overwriting findings
rationale: A deterministic recovery procedure subordinate to the routing checkpoint.

statement: launch_state is intended before the harness is executed and becomes confirmed only once the harness reports itself ready, so a harness that rejects a pin and exits never leaves evidence claiming the model ran.
trigger: a worker is launched with a pinned model
outcome: launch evidence never overstates success before the harness has actually confirmed readiness
notes: Strong precedent for the proposal's executor-aware ExecutionRecord (§13.4).
rationale: One durable evidence shape (launch_record) referenced by dispatch, recovery, and resumption alike.

statement: provider_verified says whether the invocation itself proves the provider, while variant_verified is always false today because no supported harness reports back which variant it resolved, so Sergeant records the pin without claiming it was honored.
trigger: recording what a worker actually launched with
outcome: the recorded evidence never claims more certainty than what was actually observed

statement: A resumed or recovered worker reads the same fleet record and inherits the same pin; a worker handed a tuple its harness cannot honor fails terminally rather than falling back to the ambient default.
trigger: a worker is resumed or recovered
outcome: the model pin is preserved exactly across resumption, and an unhonorable pin never silently degrades

statement: A model/variant pin fails closed in two distinct situations with a diagnostic that says which: no known transport (the harness is measured and exposes no way to pin that axis) versus unmeasured (the harness is not installed here, so its launch surface has not been observed) — the latter is not a claim the harness cannot do it.
trigger: a model/variant pin cannot be applied
outcome: the failure diagnostic distinguishes a measured incapability from simple absence of measurement
notes: A precise instance of the repo's own 'measure the CLI, never assume' doctrine applied to pin failures specifically.

statement: A coordinator not inside tmux binding a coordinator pane, whether via --managed-coordinator-pane or --coordinator-pane, still requires a persistent interactive worker and still fails before any intent file, td task, worktree, or fleet state is created.
trigger: a coordinator outside tmux needs to dispatch
outcome: the same fail-before-any-state-created guarantee holds regardless of which pane-binding path is used
notes: Adds a precondition detail (fail before state creation) to the pane-identity rule already captured from AGENTS.md L188.
rationale: Same D2 supersession as AGENTS.md's coordinator-pane unit; the durable fail-before-side-effect intent already appears as agents-invariant/stage-context elsewhere and does not need restating per mechanism.
alternatives_considered: stage-context (rejected as duplicate of the durable half already captured)

statement: The managed coordinator pane is reused across dispatches and runs a reader that only displays each line it receives and never executes it, so a tmux-injected notification can never become a shell command in the coordinator's pane.
trigger: a notification is delivered into the managed coordinator pane
outcome: delivered content can never be interpreted as an executable command
notes: A genuine security invariant (never execute injected content), but the channel it protects (tmux pane injection) does not exist in the sergeant-rs daemon at all — D2 already establishes no TTY/pane — so the property is preserved structurally rather than needing its own re-implementation.
rationale: The property this rule protects is achieved in sergeant-rs simply by the daemon having no command-execution channel reachable from notification delivery; nothing to port beyond noting the intent for provenance.
alternatives_considered: engine-gap (rejected: property already holds structurally, nothing missing to claim)

statement: Drain admission locking uses an atomic hard link rather than requiring an optional locking tool, so flock is deliberately not a prerequisite; the drain state directory must be writable and on a filesystem that supports hard links, otherwise dispatch and respond fail closed rather than proceeding unlocked.
trigger: a worker or respond action needs to check or acquire a drain admission lock
outcome: admission control uses a portable atomic primitive and fails closed if that primitive is unavailable, rather than depending on an optional external tool
notes: Portable cross-platform design fact; directly relevant to the proposal's §18 cross-platform contract despite the mechanism itself (bin/_sgt-drain.sh) being P6's.
rationale: A single locking contract reused by dispatch, respond, and recovery.

statement: Sergeant is designed for one developer per installation; adoption by a larger organization means each developer installs Sergeant independently, and one installation is never turned into a shared team service.
trigger: considering how Sergeant is deployed across a team
outcome: every installation remains single-developer-owned even at organizational scale

statement: Each installation owns its own project configuration, local Git credentials and GitHub account selection, worktrees or Treehouse leases, fleet worker state, local tmux panes and agent processes, and local wiki captures and knowledge graphs.
trigger: reasoning about what state belongs to a given installation
outcome: no installation-owned resource is ever assumed shared across machines or users
rationale: Defines the local-only ownership boundary that every workflow implicitly respects.

statement: Sergeant does not provide central tenancy, organization RBAC, shared credentials, cross-machine worker leases, or a team-wide fleet database.
trigger: considering whether a feature crosses the single-user boundary
outcome: the listed multi-tenant capabilities are explicit non-goals

statement: A Project is a named YAML configuration containing repositories, groups, roles, inherited instructions, and optional project-level Graphify output.
trigger: defining the term 'project'
outcome: the term Project has one authoritative definition reused across all procedures

statement: A Repository is one source repository with a resolved local path, optional clone URL, role, group, and repository-specific agent instructions.
trigger: defining the term 'repository'
outcome: the term Repository has one authoritative definition

statement: A Task is tracked work in the configured task adapter (currently Marcus td); a task records ownership, decisions, handoff state, review, and closure.
trigger: defining the term 'task'
outcome: the term Task has one authoritative definition including what it must record

statement: A Fleet is the local collection of dispatched workers for a Sergeant task; fleet state is operational evidence, not a replacement for Git, task, PR, or validation state.
trigger: defining the term 'fleet' and its authority
outcome: fleet state is never treated as more authoritative than the actual git/task/PR/validation state it describes
notes: Directly echoes sergeant-rs's own 'the journal is the only truth' invariant — fleet state here plays the disposable-projection role, not the source-of-truth role.

statement: A Worker is an agent running in an isolated worktree and tmux pane; a live process is not proof of progress, and recent meaningful progress evidence is required.
trigger: defining the term 'worker' and what counts as its activity
outcome: worker activity claims always require evidence of recent meaningful progress, never bare liveness
notes: The canonical source of the 'liveness is not progress' rule echoed in AGENTS.md's standard workflow (L144) and avoid-no-op list (L167-168).

statement: A Decision request is a needs_input, blocked, or validation ask-user gate that requires a human product, security, privacy, destructive-action, or risk decision; mechanical findings are not human decision requests.
trigger: distinguishing a gate that needs a human decision from one that does not
outcome: only genuinely human-authority decisions are escalated as decision requests; mechanical findings are handled without escalation
notes: Primary source evidence for the proposal's needs_input semantics investigation (U3).

statement: Direct mode is used when the user explicitly requests implementation in the current session and one repository owns the outcome; it still requires a task, TDD, repository-native checks, independent review, shipping validation, and handoff.
trigger: the trigger condition for direct mode holds
outcome: direct mode delivers through the same gates as dispatch mode, never a lighter path
notes: The authoritative summary definition; overlaps with AGENTS.md's direct-mode workflow BUs — likely merges with them at synthesis.
alternatives_considered: stage-context of the direct-mode workflow already captured from AGENTS.md

statement: Dispatch mode is used for cross-repository work, independent parallel repository tasks, isolated review workers, or an explicit request for workers; Sergeant creates isolated worktrees, injects repository instructions, and records fleet state.
trigger: the trigger condition for dispatch mode holds
outcome: dispatch mode always creates isolated worktrees, injects instructions, and records fleet state
notes: The authoritative summary definition; overlaps with AGENTS.md's dispatch-mode workflow BUs.
alternatives_considered: stage-context of the dispatch-mode workflow already captured from AGENTS.md

statement: Sergeant is not a centralized team orchestration service, not a replacement for GitHub, Git, CI, or the task tracker, and is not permission to push directly to default branches.
trigger: considering whether a capability belongs in Sergeant
outcome: the listed capabilities remain explicit non-goals regardless of convenience

statement: Sergeant does not authorize validation agents to modify source while reporting findings.
trigger: a validation/review agent is producing findings
outcome: a review agent never mutates the source it is reviewing
notes: A distinct, high-value invariant not otherwise stated this explicitly elsewhere in P1.

statement: no-mistakes validates one explicit final shipping boundary.
trigger: positioning no-mistakes among Sergeant's related tools
outcome: no-mistakes is understood as exactly one boundary, not an ongoing or repeatable check
notes: Reinforces README's no-mistakes framing (L264) from the related-tools glossary angle.

statement: Sergeant loads skills only when their trigger applies; skills are executable agent instructions, so their source should be reviewed before installing or updating them.
trigger: a skill is being loaded or installed/updated
outcome: no skill loads without its trigger applying, and none is installed/updated unreviewed
notes: Restates AGENTS.md L109 and adds a distinct install-time review requirement not present there.

statement: Skills may live in several distinct locations (this repository's skills/, .agents/skills/, .claude/skills/, opencode.json-referenced paths, and the user's global ~/.agents/skills/, ~/.claude/skills/, ~/.config/opencode/skills/), each serving a different repo-local-vs-global or harness-specific discovery purpose.
trigger: determining where a candidate skill lives and why
outcome: each skill location's purpose and discovery scope is known before treating it as authoritative

statement: Do not infer a skill's provenance from its folder name; check .skill-lock.json, a package lock, plugin metadata, or the source repository instead.
trigger: determining where a skill actually came from
outcome: provenance is established from lock/metadata evidence, never assumed from a directory name

statement: Sergeant-generated worker briefs do not require a global skill installation for their core workflow — the required worker bundle is vendored directly in this repository.
trigger: a dispatched worker needs its required skill bundle
outcome: the worker's core skill needs are met from the vendored repository tree without depending on any global install
notes: Cross-references docs/repo-scoped-skills.md, which owns the vendored-bundle inventory.

statement: The skills.sh installation route copies editable skills into Agent Skills locations, while the Claude plugin route installs a managed read-only bundle; plugin-owned files should not be edited, since updates will not preserve those edits.
trigger: an external skill was installed via the Claude plugin route
outcome: edits are never made to plugin-owned skill files, since they will be silently lost on update

statement: load-project, cross-repo-work, dispatch, wiki, sergeant-help, sergeant-setup, and to-tickets are Sergeant-owned skills, each with an explicit named trigger, governed by this repository's own tests and review.
trigger: determining which skills are Sergeant-owned versus externally sourced
outcome: Sergeant-owned skills are identified as a closed, repository-governed set distinct from externally installed ones
notes: Substantially duplicates AGENTS.md's procedural-skills table (L111-118) but additionally lists to-tickets; likely merges with it at synthesis.
alternatives_considered: stage-context of the standard workflow's mode-selection stage

statement: Skills split into user-invoked orchestrators, which the user selects explicitly and which may in turn drive model-invoked disciplines, versus model-invoked disciplines, which load automatically whenever the task matches.

source.locator: docs/skills.md L88-100, orchestrator vs discipline distinction

trigger: determining whether a skill should be explicitly selected or auto-loaded
outcome: the same closed two-way distinction governs how every skill in the catalog is invoked
notes: The individual skill/trigger rows in this table are secondary index entries; their primary source is each skill's own SKILL.md, owned by P2/P3/P4 — not re-extracted here to avoid duplicating those partitions.

statement: Before adopting an external skill, it must be vetted through a fixed sequence: read its complete SKILL.md and referenced scripts, confirm its source and update mechanism, check its filesystem/shell/network/git/credential actions, verify it does not conflict with repository AGENTS.md or safety policy, pin or lock its source where supported, and test it in a disposable repository or worktree before broad installation.
trigger: adopting a new external skill not already vetted
outcome: no external skill is broadly installed without having passed every step of this sequence
rationale: Recognizable trigger (adopting an external skill), bounded ordered outcome (vetted-or-rejected), and a clear completion condition — a genuine reusable procedure distinct from a single invariant.
alternatives_considered: agents-invariant (too coarse; misses the ordered checkpoint structure)

statement: Read the external skill's complete SKILL.md and referenced scripts before adopting it.
trigger: vet-external-skill workflow entered
outcome: the skill's full instructions and scripts are read, not sampled

statement: Confirm the external skill's source and update mechanism.
trigger: step 1 complete
outcome: provenance and update path are known before proceeding

statement: Check the external skill's filesystem, shell, network, Git, and credential actions.
trigger: source confirmed
outcome: the skill's side-effect surface across five named categories is known

statement: Verify the external skill does not conflict with repository AGENTS.md or safety policy.
trigger: actions checked
outcome: no adopted skill contradicts the repository's own instruction or safety policy

statement: Pin or lock the external skill's source where the installer supports it.
trigger: no conflict found
outcome: the installed skill version is pinned wherever the tooling allows

statement: Test the external skill in a disposable repository or worktree before broad installation.
trigger: source pinned
outcome: the skill is proven in an isolated environment before being broadly installed

statement: For skills.sh-managed skills, rerun the official installer and inspect the diff and updated lock file before accepting changes.
trigger: updating a skills.sh-managed skill
outcome: no update is accepted without inspecting its diff and lock-file change first
rationale: An update-time re-check of the same vetting discipline, not a fully separate procedure.

statement: For Sergeant-owned skills, update this repository through a reviewed PR and run tests/instruction-policy-test.sh plus the full Sergeant test suite.
trigger: updating a Sergeant-owned skill
outcome: no Sergeant-owned skill changes ship without passing review and the full test suite, including the instruction-policy test
notes: Directly names tests/instruction-policy-test.sh, owned by P7 — good cross-partition evidence link.
rationale: Distinct from the external-skill vetting workflow (this is Sergeant's own change-review discipline), but analogous enough to record alongside it; flagged for synthesis to decide whether it deserves its own workflow.
alternatives_considered: separate workflow: 'update-sergeant-owned-skill'

statement: Sergeant vendors the workflow skills required by generated worker briefs directly in .agents/skills/, the canonical Agent Skills tree discovered directly by Codex, with OpenCode discovering the same tree via opencode.json and Claude discovering it only through repository-local links in .claude/skills/ — no install step writes to a user's global agent configuration.
trigger: a worker brief needs its required skills discovered by any of the three supported harnesses
outcome: every harness resolves the same vendored, repository-local skill tree, and nothing Sergeant does ever writes to global agent configuration
rationale: The 'no install step writes to global config' clause is a strong isolation invariant worth preserving explicitly.

statement: The worker-brief skill inventory is a fixed named set (code-review, codebase-design, diagnosing-bugs, domain-modeling, grill-with-docs, grilling, implement, no-mistakes, prototype, research, resolving-merge-conflicts, tdd, to-spec, to-tickets, triage, wayfinder) vendored under .agents/skills/.
trigger: determining which skills a generated worker brief may reference
outcome: worker briefs draw only from this fixed, vendored inventory
notes: Each individual skill's behavior is owned by P2/P3/P4/P5's own SKILL.md extraction; this unit records only the index/inventory fact.

statement: sergeant-setup is also vendored under .agents/skills/ but is not required by generated worker briefs — it is a Sergeant-authored installation/repair skill, not a worker-brief dependency.
trigger: distinguishing worker-brief-required skills from other vendored ones
outcome: sergeant-setup is never assumed necessary for a generated worker brief to function

statement: Workers are instructed never to invoke no-mistakes directly; the skill is vendored only so workers can load and understand the coordinator-owned shipping gate contract when a brief references it.
trigger: a worker's brief references no-mistakes
outcome: the worker can understand the contract without ever being able to invoke the gate itself
notes: The clearest single statement of *why* no-mistakes is vendored despite workers never invoking it; reinforces AGENTS.md L152 and README L277.
